newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds baulk at 5.75 pct barrier.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds baulk at 5.75 pct barrier.

text.p: Belgian benchmark 10-year yields are bogged down in the region of 5.75 percent and it will take a fresh wave of economic data or EMU-related speculation to get them moving again, dealers said on Friday.

The bulk of them opted for a swing back towards six percent, a level where some buying might seen. The chances of that happening in the near term looked remote, though, despite major U.S. features on the market's diary -- the July 1-2 FOMC meeting on U.S. rates and the July 3 release of the June jobs report.
Dealers predicted some near-term volatility, but no major change of direction.
Dealers said OLO movements would be closely tied to Bunds, which were being rated as dear.
Market swings might be exaggerated in the next two months as holiday-related absences depleted volumes, they noted.
"We find Bunds are expensive. Looking at the range over the last six months we are trading close to the bottom in yields," ABN-AMRO said in its market comment ABKR.

"However, this is mainly a trader-dominated market with clients being absent...we feel several short squeezes have lead us to this current level. We still advise clients to hedge with options," it added.
"Judging by the behaviour of Belgian investors this rally will end soon...outright selling or selling of calls is what they have in mind," the Degroof Luxembourg comment said DELW.

"Yields of...5.75 percent on OLOs are strong points below which the markets lose their attraction...with interest rates in Japan rising and T-bonds hesitating, the European markets should start correcting," it added.

"The complete absence of end-investors makes the positive picture a fragile one...lots of investors missed the last rally, perhaps they can earn some extra return on the back of a possible downward move," Kredietbank commented.

Dealers said that once Bund futures hit 102.00 a wave of profit-taking might emerge. The contracts were at 101.93 at 1415 GMT, up 0.06. The day's high was 101.98. OLO futures were up 0.02 at 121.15, little changed from the morning levels.
One trader reported activity at the short end of the curve, where the spread against short German paper was being played. One- to three-year paper outperformed the rest of the OLO curve.

"Elsewhere Belgians are playing Bunds more actively than OLOs," he said. He was one of few traders proclaiming OLO yields could fall further. "I can't see where inflation could come from," he said, explaining his bullishness.
He predicted investors would swing back out of equities into bonds as shares ran out of upward potential.
